cards.front: Latissimus dorsi transfer for rotator cuff tears is appropriate in patients with irreparable cuff tears of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus .
cards.extra: Irreparable rotator cuff tears Superior displacement of the humeral head (AHI<5-7 mm) - acromio-humeral interval Goutallier stage 3-4 of rotator cuff muscles Increased duration of tear Substantial ER weakness Gerber et al. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24196461/) performed a case series analysis of 67 patients with irreparable rotator cuff tears managed with latissimus dorsi transfer. Patients with an intact subscapularis demonstrated improvement in pain, range of motion and strength postoperatively, while no improvement was noted in patients with subscapularis deficiency. The authors conclude that latissimus dorsi transfer should not be performed in the setting of poor subscapularis function.
